title: Sports Therapy for Resource Promotion and Support in Children and Adolescents with Chronic Diseases
summary:
Background
Many children and adolescents live with a chronic condition affecting, for example, the heart, kidneys, lungs, metabolism, or nervous system. In daily life, affected children and adolescents are often considerably less physically active than their healthy peers, even though regular physical activity is particularly important for their development. Many children with chronic conditions do not meet national and international physical activity guidelines of an average of 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per day.

Research Question
This study investigates whether a modular exercise programme, tailored specifically to children and adolescents with chronic conditions, can help increase their everyday physical activity and bring them closer to the recommended level of 60 minutes per day. In addition, the study examines whether the exercise programme improves participating children's physical performance, wellbeing, and quality of life, and whether the programme is safe and feasible to implement.

Methodology
At six pediatric hospitals in Germany, children and adolescents aged 6 to 18 years receive an individually tailored exercise programme over a period of six months. This programme comprises regular, supervised exercise sessions (on average twice weekly for 30 minutes each), supplemented by personal counselling sessions, home-based exercise instructions, and, depending on individual needs, additional components such as joint sports activities or support in returning to school and club sports. Children are supervised by sports therapists and sports scientists. Prior to the start of the programme, as well as after three, six, and twelve months, various assessments and questionnaires are administered to capture participants' everyday activity levels, physical performance, and wellbeing. Comparisons are conducted within the participating children themselves (i.e., using a within-subject design).
conditions: Due to the heterogeneity and broad diversity of the included disease entities, no specific ICD or Orpha codes are provided. The study does not focus on a single defined disease but includes children and adolescents with physician-diagnosed chronic conditions from various medical disciplines, provided that study participation is medically justifiable.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Study cohort:
•	Age: ≥ 6 and < 18 years at the time of study enrollment
•	Presence of a physician-diagnosed chronic condition or a condition with a high risk of chronification, particularly from one of the following disease areas:
o	Renal diseases
o	Metabolic diseases
o	Hematological diseases
o	Chronic pulmonary diseases
o	Cardiovascular diseases
o	Neurological/neuromuscular diseases
o	Immunological and autoimmune diseases
o	Gastroenterological diseases
o	Endocrinological diseases
•	Sufficient physical capacity to participate in a movement-related counseling/intervention program, defined as the ability to walk independently without assistive devices for at least 2 consecutive minutes
•	Insufficient physical activity, defined as not meeting the WHO physical activity recommendations for children and adolescents, i.e., averaging less than 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per day over the week
•	Presence of a medical certificate of fitness/medical clearance to participate in the study and in movement-related programs
•	Written informed consent from at least one legal guardian (for participants <18 years of age)
•	Written informed consent from the study participant
•	Sufficient German language proficiency of the child/adolescent and at least one legal guardian, such that study information, consent forms, questionnaires, and safety-relevant instructions can be understood

Inclusion Criteria (Care Cohort)
•	Age: ≥ 3 and < 18 years at the time of study enrollment. 
•	Physician-diagnosed chronic disease or a condition associated with a high risk of chronicity, particularly within one of the following disease categories: 
o	Kidney diseases 
o	Metabolic diseases 
o	Hematological diseases 
o	Chronic pulmonary diseases 
o	Cardiovascular diseases 
o	Neurological/neuromuscular diseases 
o	Immunological and autoimmune diseases 
o	Gastroenterological diseases 
o	Endocrine diseases 
•	Other chronic diseases or health-related impairments, as determined by the treating physician, provided that study participation is considered medically appropriate. 
•	Ability to ambulate with or without assistive devices, or wheelchair mobility with the ability to actively participate. 
•	Medical clearance confirming that participation in the exercise modules and exercise interventions is safe. 
•	Written informed consent from at least one parent/legal guardian (participants <18 years). 
•	Written informed assent/consent from the study participant (participants >7 years). 
•	Sufficient language proficiency of the child/adolescent and at least one parent/legal guardian to ensure understanding of study information, informed consent documents, questionnaires, and safety-related instructions.
Exclusion criteria:
Study cohort:
•	Age: < 6 or ≥ 18 years at the time of study enrollment
•	No physician-diagnosed chronic condition and no condition with a high risk of chronification
•	Acute oncological diseases
•	Exclusive presence of a primary psychiatric, neuropsychological, or developmental diagnosis without an additional chronic somatic disease or without any other condition carrying a high risk of chronification, e.g., depression, anxiety disorder, somatization disorder, ADHD, or autism spectrum disorder
•	Meeting the WHO physical activity recommendations for children and adolescents, i.e., averaging at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per day over the week
•	Medical, cognitive, motor, neurological, neuromuscular, pulmonary, cardiac, metabolic, or psychiatric limitations that, according to medical or study-related assessment, do not permit safe performance of the assessments or the movement-related intervention. Examples: unstable health status, insufficiently stabilized severe psychiatric illness, severe metabolic derangements, severe cardiac or pulmonary exercise limitations, pronounced motor or cognitive impairments precluding feasibility of testing
•	Acute medical contraindication to physical activity or physical exertion, e.g., acute infection, febrile illness, acute injury, acute decompensation of the underlying condition, or a physician-determined contraindication to exertion (inclusion possible after resolution of the acute condition)
•	Inability to walk, or ability to walk only with assistive devices, or ability to walk without assistive devices for less than 2 consecutive minutes
•	Absent or insufficient provision of assistive devices, insofar as this compromises the mobility, safety, or feasibility required for study participation
•	Concurrent participation in another clinical study or intervention investigating physical activity, movement behavior, physical performance, or comparable movement-related outcomes, or in which mutual influence on study results cannot be ruled out

Care cohort:
•	Age: < 3 or ≥ 18 years at the time of study enrollment. 
•	No physician-diagnosed chronic disease and no condition associated with a high risk of chronicity. 
•	Acute oncological disease. 
•	Presence of an exclusively psychiatric, neuropsychological, or developmental diagnosis without an additional chronic somatic disease or another condition associated with a high risk of chronicity, e.g., depression, anxiety disorder, somatic symptom disorder, ADHD, or autism spectrum disorder. 
•	Medical, cognitive, motor, neurological, neuromuscular, pulmonary, cardiac, metabolic, or psychiatric impairments that, in the opinion of the treating physician or the study team, preclude the safe implementation of the exercise intervention. Examples include an unstable medical condition, insufficiently stabilized severe psychiatric illness, severe metabolic decompensation, severe cardiac or pulmonary exercise limitations, or pronounced motor or cognitive impairments preventing participation in the interventions. 
•	Acute medical contraindication to physical activity or exercise, acute decompensation of the underlying disease, or physician-determined contraindication to exercise. 
•	Inadequate provision of assistive devices preventing the implementation of the interventions. 
•	Missing or insufficient assistive devices if the required mobility, safety, or feasibility for study participation cannot be ensured.
